q: 这是医生___药，不是我的。
zh: 这是医生的药，不是我的。
py: zhè shì yī shēng de yào bú shì wǒ de
en: This is the doctor's medicine, not mine.
why: An owner noun before an ordinary thing needs 的: 医生的药. 地 and 得 attach to verbs and adjectives, and 医生药 with nothing between sounds like a compound, not 'the doctor's medicine'.

q: 我借了弟弟___耳机。
zh: 我借了弟弟的耳机。
py: wǒ jiè le dì di de ěr jī
en: I borrowed my younger brother's earphones.
why: 弟弟 is the owner and 耳机 is an ordinary thing he owns, so 的 links them. With nothing there, 弟弟耳机 does not read as 'brother's earphones'. 得 and 地 never link a noun to a noun.

q: 请把老师___邮箱地址发给我。
zh: 请把老师的邮箱地址发给我。
py: qǐng bǎ lǎo shī de yóu xiāng dì zhǐ fā gěi wǒ
en: Please send me the teacher's email address.
why: Owner + 的 + thing: 老师的邮箱地址. 的 is the only one of these that joins a possessor to a noun; 得 and 地 follow verbs and adjectives.

q: 护士___手机一直占线，我打不通。
zh: 护士的手机一直占线，我打不通。
py: hù shi de shǒu jī yì zhí zhàn xiàn wǒ dǎ bù tōng
en: The nurse's phone has been busy all the time; I can't get through.
why: The noun 护士 owns the 手机, so 的 goes between them. 护士地手机 and 护士得手机 misuse the other two de's, which belong to adverbs and complements.

q: 邻居___路由器坏了，所以他来借我们的网络。
zh: 邻居的路由器坏了，所以他来借我们的网络。
py: lín jū de lù yóu qì huài le suǒ yǐ tā lái jiè wǒ men de wǎng luò
en: The neighbour's router broke, so he came to use our internet.
why: Noun owner + 的 + thing: 邻居的路由器. The English 's has no Chinese ending other than 的, and leaving it out makes 邻居路由器 sound like a product type.

q: 听说那位医生___诊所在老城区，离地铁站不太远。
zh: 听说那位医生的诊所在老城区，离地铁站不太远。
py: tīng shuō nà wèi yī shēng de zhěn suǒ zài lǎo chéng qū lí dì tiě zhàn bù tài yuǎn
en: I hear that doctor's clinic is in the old town, not far from the metro station.
why: The owner is the whole phrase 那位医生, and 的 closes it before the thing owned: 那位医生的诊所. Without 的 the phrase 医生诊所 would lose the possessor meaning.

q: 同事___笔记本电脑没电了，我把我的充电器借给了他。
zh: 同事的笔记本电脑没电了，我把我的充电器借给了他。
py: tóng shì de bǐ jì běn diàn nǎo méi diàn le wǒ bǎ wǒ de chōng diàn qì jiè gěi le tā
en: My colleague's laptop ran out of battery, so I lent him my charger.
why: 同事 owns the laptop, so 同事的笔记本电脑. A long noun like 笔记本电脑 after a bare owner is not a tight pair, so 的 is needed to mark the owner.

q: 医生检查了我爷爷___眼睛，说没有大问题。
zh: 医生检查了我爷爷的眼睛，说没有大问题。
py: yī shēng jiǎn chá le wǒ yé ye de yǎn jing shuō méi yǒu dà wèn tí
en: The doctor examined my grandfather's eyes and said there was no big problem.
why: In a chain, 的 is dropped after the pronoun (我爷爷) but kept on the last link before the thing: 我爷爷的眼睛. Here 眼睛 is a body part in object position, so the link 的 stays.

q: 护士量了我奶奶___血压，一切都正常。
zh: 护士量了我奶奶的血压，一切都正常。
py: hù shi liáng le wǒ nǎi nai de xuè yā yī qiè dōu zhèng cháng
en: The nurse measured my grandmother's blood pressure; everything was normal.
why: The pronoun 我 attaches to 奶奶 with no 的, but 奶奶 + 血压 is owner + thing, so 的 comes after 奶奶: 我奶奶的血压. 得 and 地 do not link nouns.

q: 我姐姐___医生朋友告诉我，多喝水对嗓子有好处。
zh: 我姐姐的医生朋友告诉我，多喝水对嗓子有好处。
py: wǒ jiě jie de yī shēng péng you gào sù wǒ duō hē shuǐ duì sǎng zi yǒu hǎo chù
en: A doctor friend of my older sister's told me drinking more water is good for the throat.
why: 我姐姐 keeps no 的 after the pronoun, but the chain ends with 的 before the noun 医生朋友: 我姐姐的医生朋友. 得 and 地 cannot link two nouns.

q: 医生看了看我弟弟___牙齿。
zh: 医生看了看我弟弟的牙齿。
py: yī shēng kàn le kàn wǒ dì di de yá chǐ
en: The doctor looked at my younger brother's teeth.
why: Family member + thing: the 的 after 弟弟 stays, since 牙齿 is a thing owned. Only the 的 right after the pronoun 我 is dropped.

q: 她是一个很好___朋友，生病时总是陪着我。
zh: 她是一个很好的朋友，生病时总是陪着我。
py: tā shì yí gè hěn hǎo de péng you shēng bìng shí zǒng shì péi zhe wǒ
en: She is a very good friend; she always stays with me when I'm ill.
why: 很 + adjective is a phrase, so 的 is required before the noun: 很好的朋友. 好朋友 without 很 is fine, but 很好朋友 is not. 地 and 得 are for verbs.

q: 我想买一部很小___手机。
zh: 我想买一部很小的手机。
py: wǒ xiǎng mǎi yī bù hěn xiǎo de shǒu jī
en: I want to buy a very small phone.
why: Once 很 is in front of the adjective, 的 must link it to 手机: 很小的手机. Dropping it works only for a bare one-syllable adjective like 小手机.

q: 这是一家非常大___医院，每天有几千个病人。
zh: 这是一家非常大的医院，每天有几千个病人。
py: zhè shì yī jiā fēi cháng dà de yī yuàn měi tiān yǒu jǐ qiān gè bìng rén
en: This is a very big hospital, with thousands of patients every day.
why: 非常 + 大 is a degree phrase, so it needs 的: 非常大的医院. 非常大医院 is wrong, and 大得 / 大地 would be a complement or adverb, not a noun modifier.

q: 我想找一个安静___地方打电话。
zh: 我想找一个安静的地方打电话。
py: wǒ xiǎng zhǎo yí gè ān jìng de dì fang dǎ diàn huà
en: I want to find a quiet place to make a call.
why: 安静 has two syllables, so it takes 的 before the noun: 安静的地方. The 地 in 地方 is part of the noun, so 安静地方 is read wrongly, and 安静地 would be an adverb.

q: 医生给我开了一些很苦___药。
zh: 医生给我开了一些很苦的药。
py: yī shēng gěi wǒ kāi le yī xiē hěn kǔ de yào
en: The doctor prescribed me some very bitter medicine.
why: 一些 + 很苦 + 药: the adjective has a degree word, so 的 is required: 很苦的药. 苦得药 and 苦地药 use the wrong de.

q: 网速特别慢___时候，视频总是停下来。
zh: 网速特别慢的时候，视频总是停下来。
py: wǎng sù tè bié màn de shí hou shì pín zǒng shì tíng xià lái
en: When the internet is very slow, videos keep stopping.
why: 特别慢 is a phrase describing 时候, so it needs 的: 特别慢的时候. 慢得 would introduce a result complement, which this clause does not have.

q: 他买了一部又轻又薄___手机。
zh: 他买了一部又轻又薄的手机。
py: tā mǎi le yī bù yòu qīng yòu báo de shǒu jī
en: He bought a phone that is both light and thin.
why: 又轻又薄 is a multi-word description, so 的 links it to 手机. Bare adjectives drop 的 only when a single one-syllable adjective stands alone.

q: 她是一个认真、耐心、对病人非常温柔___护士。
zh: 她是一个认真、耐心、对病人非常温柔的护士。
py: tā shì yí gè rèn zhēn nài xīn duì bìng rén fēi cháng wēn róu de hù shi
en: She is a serious, patient nurse who is very gentle with patients.
why: A long description made of several parts, including 对病人非常温柔, must close with 的 before 护士. 地 would turn the phrase into an adverb of manner.

q: 这是我用过的最方便___软件，不用注册就能看。
zh: 这是我用过的最方便的软件，不用注册就能看。
py: zhè shì wǒ yòng guò de zuì fāng biàn de ruǎn jiàn bù yòng zhù cè jiù néng kàn
en: This is the most convenient software I have used; you can watch without registering.
why: 最 + adjective needs 的 before the noun: 最方便的软件. The earlier 的 in 用过的 makes a relative clause, and both 的 are required, one for each description.

q: 我昨天下载___软件是免费的。
zh: 我昨天下载的软件是免费的。
py: wǒ zuó tiān xià zài de ruǎn jiàn shì miǎn fèi de
en: The software I downloaded yesterday is free.
why: A clause that describes a noun ends in 的: 我昨天下载的软件. Putting 了 there would leave 我昨天下载了软件 as a full sentence followed by an unrelated 是免费的.

q: 这是医生给我开___药。
zh: 这是医生给我开的药。
py: zhè shì yī shēng gěi wǒ kāi de yào
en: This is the medicine the doctor prescribed for me.
why: 'The medicine the doctor prescribed' is the clause 医生给我开 + 的 + the noun 药. There is no word for 'that', and 了 inside the clause would break the noun phrase.

q: 喜欢玩游戏___人很多。
zh: 喜欢玩游戏的人很多。
py: xǐ huan wán yóu xì de rén hěn duō
en: There are many people who like playing games.
why: A verb phrase can describe a noun: 喜欢玩游戏 + 的 + 人. The clause comes before 人, and 的 closes it. 地 or 得 would turn it into an adverb or a complement.

q: 你昨天在网上买___充电器到了吗？
zh: 你昨天在网上买的充电器到了吗？
py: nǐ zuó tiān zài wǎng shàng mǎi de chōng diàn qì dào le ma
en: Has the charger you bought online yesterday arrived?
why: 'The charger you bought' needs 的 after the clause 你昨天在网上买. 了, 着 and 过 would make 买 a closed verb phrase and leave 充电器到了吗 without a proper subject.

q: 医生说，经常熬夜___人容易头疼。
zh: 医生说，经常熬夜的人容易头疼。
py: yī shēng shuō jīng cháng áo yè de rén róng yì tóu téng
en: The doctor says people who often stay up late get headaches easily.
why: 经常熬夜 describes the noun 人, so the clause takes 的: 经常熬夜的人. 熬夜得 would expect a result complement, which is not what follows.

q: 我们去看病___那家医院可以在手机上挂号。
zh: 我们去看病的那家医院可以在手机上挂号。
py: wǒ men qù kàn bìng de nà jiā yī yuàn kě yǐ zài shǒu jī shàng guà hào
en: The hospital where we go to see the doctor lets you register on your phone.
why: 去看病 is a clause describing 医院, so 的 closes it: 去看病的那家医院. The clause comes before the noun and the 那家 stays right in front of 医院.

q: 睡觉前看手机___习惯对眼睛不好。
zh: 睡觉前看手机的习惯对眼睛不好。
py: shuì jiào qián kàn shǒu jī de xí guàn duì yǎn jing bù hǎo
en: The habit of looking at your phone before bed is bad for the eyes.
why: A whole verb phrase can describe 习惯: 睡觉前看手机 + 的 + 习惯. Without 的 the phrase would sound like two actions, and 了 would add a completed event the habit does not have.

q: 修手机___地方在二楼。
zh: 修手机的地方在二楼。
py: xiū shǒu jī de dì fang zài èr lóu
en: The place where they fix phones is on the second floor.
why: 修手机 + 的 + 地方 gives 'the place where (they) fix phones'. 地 is not an option because the noun 地方 already starts right after the blank.

q: 我每天用来记录睡眠___那个软件，最近突然不能用了。
zh: 我每天用来记录睡眠的那个软件，最近突然不能用了。
py: wǒ měi tiān yòng lái jì lù shuì mián de nà ge ruǎn jiàn zuì jìn tū rán bù néng yòng le
en: The software I use every day to track my sleep suddenly stopped working recently.
why: 记录睡眠 describes 那个软件, and the clause closes with 的 before the 那个 + noun. The 了 later in the sentence belongs to the main verb and cannot be borrowed inside the clause.

q: 昨天在医院门口遇到___那位老人是我们小区的邻居。
zh: 昨天在医院门口遇到的那位老人是我们小区的邻居。
py: zuó tiān zài yī yuàn mén kǒu yù dào de nà wèi lǎo rén shì wǒ men xiǎo qū de lín jū
en: The elderly man I met at the hospital entrance yesterday is a neighbour from our community.
why: With 的 the clause 昨天在医院门口遇到 describes 那位老人. With 了 the clause would be a finished event and 那位老人是…邻居 would have no proper subject.

q: 医生让我把最近每天吃___东西都写下来。
zh: 医生让我把最近每天吃的东西都写下来。
py: yī shēng ràng wǒ bǎ zuì jìn měi tiān chī de dōng xi dōu xiě xià lái
en: The doctor asked me to write down everything I have eaten each day lately.
why: 每天吃 + 的 + 东西 is 'the things (I) eat every day'. 了 in the clause would not combine with the habit 每天, and 地 or 得 do not modify nouns.

q: 这个充电器不是我___，是弟弟的。
zh: 这个充电器不是我的，是弟弟的。
py: zhè ge chōng diàn qì bú shì wǒ de shì dì di de
en: This charger isn't mine; it's my brother's.
why: The noun 充电器 is already mentioned, so 我的 means 'mine'. Dropping 的 gives 不是我, which says the charger is not me.

q: 这两部手机，大___是我的，小的是姐姐的。
zh: 这两部手机，大的是我的，小的是姐姐的。
py: zhè liǎng bù shǒu jī dà de shì wǒ de xiǎo de shì jiě jie de
en: Of these two phones, the big one is mine and the small one is my sister's.
why: The noun 手机 is understood, so 大 + 的 means 'the big one'. 大个 or 大些 would not mean that, and bare 大 cannot stand as a noun here.

q: 医生说我不能喝冷___，只能喝热的。
zh: 医生说我不能喝冷的，只能喝热的。
py: yī shēng shuō wǒ bù néng hē lěng de zhǐ néng hē rè de
en: The doctor says I can't drink cold things, only hot ones.
why: 喝冷 alone is incomplete; 冷的 means 'something cold'. The same 的 appears in 热的, so the two halves match.

q: 这副耳机是谁___？
zh: 这副耳机是谁的？
py: zhè fù ěr jī shì shéi de
en: Whose earphones are these?
why: 谁的 means 'whose', and the noun 耳机 is already in the question, so 的 stays. 这副耳机是谁 would ask who the earphones are.

q: 我的手机屏幕太小了，我想换一个大___。
zh: 我的手机屏幕太小了，我想换一个大的。
py: wǒ de shǒu jī píng mù tài xiǎo le wǒ xiǎng huàn yí gè dà de
en: My phone screen is too small; I want to switch to a bigger one.
why: 'A big one' is 大的, with 的 standing for the missing 手机. English 'one' is not added again, and 换一个大 alone is incomplete.

q: 出门前带点吃___，路上可能会饿。
zh: 出门前带点吃的，路上可能会饿。
py: chū mén qián dài diǎn chī de lù shàng kě néng huì è
en: Take something to eat before you go out; you may get hungry on the way.
why: 吃的 means 'something to eat', with 的 turning the verb into a thing. 带点吃 is not complete, and 吃了 would be a completed action instead.

q: 这不是医生给我开___，是我自己在药店买的。
zh: 这不是医生给我开的，是我自己在药店买的。
py: zhè bú shì yī shēng gěi wǒ kāi de shì wǒ zì jǐ zài yào diàn mǎi de
en: This isn't what the doctor prescribed for me; I bought it myself at the pharmacy.
why: The noun 药 is dropped, so the clause 医生给我开 keeps 的: 医生给我开的 = 'what the doctor prescribed'. 了 would make the clause complete and the meaning changes.

q: 这个手机壳不是我买___，是朋友送的。
zh: 这个手机壳不是我买的，是朋友送的。
py: zhè ge shǒu jī ké bú shì wǒ mǎi de shì péng you sòng de
en: I didn't buy this phone case; a friend gave it to me.
why: 不是我买的 means 'it is not what I bought', with 的 marking the clause as a description with no noun. 了, 过 and 着 do not work after 不是.

q: 这两种药，我要饭后吃___。
zh: 这两种药，我要饭后吃的。
py: zhè liǎng zhǒng yào wǒ yào fàn hòu chī de
en: Of these two medicines, I want the one that is taken after meals.
why: 饭后吃的 means 'the one taken after meals', and 的 stands for 药. Without it, 我要饭后吃 would mean 'I want to eat after meals', which is not the cue.

q: 我的手机坏了，用姐姐___吧，她今天不用。
zh: 我的手机坏了，用姐姐的吧，她今天不用。
py: wǒ de shǒu jī huài le yòng jiě jie de ba tā jīn tiān bù yòng
en: My phone is broken; use my sister's, she isn't using it today.
why: 姐姐的 means 'my sister's (phone)'. The noun 手机 is already known, so 的 stays alone. 用姐姐 would mean 'use my sister'.

q: 我弟弟买了___很好的手机。
zh: 我弟弟买了一部很好的手机。
py: wǒ dì di mǎi le yī bù hěn hǎo de shǒu jī
en: My younger brother bought a very good phone.
why: A new thing is introduced with 一 + measure word before the description: 一部很好的手机. 的 never follows the measure word, and 这部 would make the phone a known one.

q: ___朋友今天都生病了。
zh: 我的两个朋友今天都生病了。
py: wǒ de liǎng gè péng you jīn tiān dōu shēng bìng le
en: Two of my friends are sick today.
why: The owner goes before the number: 我的两个朋友. English 'two of my friends' tempts you to say 两个我的朋友, which Chinese does not allow.

q: 我昨天在医院认识了___。
zh: 我昨天在医院认识了一位很有耐心的护士。
py: wǒ zuó tiān zài yī yuàn rèn shi le yī wèi hěn yǒu nài xīn de hù shi
en: I met a very patient nurse at the hospital yesterday.
why: 一位 comes first, then the description 很有耐心 + 的, then the noun. 的 belongs right before 护士, not after 一位, and 很有耐心 needs it.

q: 我昨天买的___手机，今天就坏了。
zh: 我昨天买的那部手机，今天就坏了。
py: wǒ zuó tiān mǎi de nà bù shǒu jī jīn tiān jiù huài le
en: The phone I bought yesterday broke today already.
why: After the clause + 的, 那部 sits directly before 手机: 我昨天买的那部手机. 的 does not come after a measure word, so 那部的 is wrong.

q: 你认识___会修手机的人吗？
zh: 你认识一个会修手机的人吗？
py: nǐ rèn shi yí gè huì xiū shǒu jī de rén ma
en: Do you know a person who can fix phones?
why: 一个 comes directly before the described noun with no 的 in between: 一个会修手机的人. The 的 that is needed sits after 会修手机, not after the measure word.

q: 他给我推荐了___很实用的健康软件。
zh: 他给我推荐了一个很实用的健康软件。
py: tā gěi wǒ tuī jiàn le yí gè hěn shí yòng de jiàn kāng ruǎn jiàn
en: He recommended a very practical health app to me.
why: The new item is 一个 + description + 的 + noun, so 一个很实用的健康软件. 一个的 puts 的 straight after the measure word, which is wrong, and 这个 would make it already known.

q: 我有三个___朋友在医院工作。
zh: 我有三个朋友在医院工作。
py: wǒ yǒu sān gè péng you zài yī yuàn gōng zuò
en: I have three friends who work in a hospital.
why: Number + measure word attaches straight to the noun: 三个朋友. 的 never goes after 个, even though English 'three of' might suggest a link.

q: 请给我一杯___热水。
zh: 请给我一杯热水。
py: qǐng gěi wǒ yī bēi rè shuǐ
en: Please give me a glass of hot water.
why: 一杯热水 has no 的 after the measure word 杯. The adjective 热 is a single bare syllable, so no other 的 is needed either.

q: 这个___手机是谁的？
zh: 这个手机是谁的？
py: zhè ge shǒu jī shì shéi de
en: Whose phone is this?
why: 这 + measure word points directly at the noun, so 这个手机 takes no 的. The 的 you do need is in 谁的 at the end.

q: 我最近睡不好，想问医生几个___问题。
zh: 我最近睡不好，想问医生几个问题。
py: wǒ zuì jìn shuì bù hǎo xiǎng wèn yī shēng jǐ gè wèn tí
en: I haven't been sleeping well lately and want to ask the doctor a few questions.
why: 几个 is a number + measure word, and nothing goes between it and 问题. 几个的问题 would suggest a sub-type of question and is not what is meant.

q: 那张___照片是我用新手机拍的。
zh: 那张照片是我用新手机拍的。
py: nà zhāng zhào piān shì wǒ yòng xīn shǒu jī pāi de
en: That photo was taken with my new phone.
why: 那张 + 照片 is a demonstrative + measure word + noun and needs no 的. 的 would only be possible after a clause, as in 我拍的那张照片.

q: 这两个___孩子今天都发烧了。
zh: 这两个孩子今天都发烧了。
py: zhè liǎng gè hái zi jīn tiān dōu fā shāo le
en: These two children both have a fever today.
why: 这两个 is a demonstrative + number + measure word, which joins the noun directly. 的 after 个 is the classic error, as in 这两个的孩子.

q: 医生给我开了一些___药，说每天饭后吃就行。
zh: 医生给我开了一些药，说每天饭后吃就行。
py: yī shēng gěi wǒ kāi le yī xiē yào shuō měi tiān fàn hòu chī jiù xíng
en: The doctor prescribed me some medicine and said to take it after meals every day.
why: 一些 works like a measure word, so 药 follows it directly: 一些药. 一些的药 is wrong; a 的 here would have to come after a descriptive phrase, not after 一些.

q: 我买了一台___很轻的笔记本电脑，带着上班很方便。
zh: 我买了一台很轻的笔记本电脑，带着上班很方便。
py: wǒ mǎi le yī tái hěn qīng de bǐ jì běn diàn nǎo dài zhe shàng bān hěn fāng biàn
en: I bought a very light laptop; it is convenient to take to work.
why: The order is 一台 + 很轻的 + 笔记本电脑. The blank sits after the measure word, so nothing goes there; the 的 belongs after 很轻.

zh: 这是医生的手机。
py: zhè shì yī shēng de shǒu jī
en: This is the doctor's phone.
why: Owner + 的 + thing: 医生的手机. The learner has to place 的 between the noun owner and the thing owned, not before 医生 or after 手机.

zh: 我奶奶的血压有点高。
py: wǒ nǎi nai de xuè yā yǒu diǎn gāo
en: My grandmother's blood pressure is a bit high.
why: Pronoun + kin takes no 的 (我奶奶), then 的 links the kin to the thing owned (的血压). 有点 stays in front of the adjective 高.

zh: 我爸爸的同事推荐的医生很有名。
py: wǒ bà ba de tóng shì tuī jiàn de yī shēng hěn yǒu míng
en: The doctor my father's colleague recommended is very famous.
why: The chain 我爸爸的同事 keeps one 的 before 同事, and the relative clause 同事推荐 takes its own 的 before 医生. The whole phrase sits before the predicate 很有名.

zh: 她是一个很细心的护士。
py: tā shì yí gè hěn xì xīn de hù shi
en: She is a very careful nurse.
why: 一个 + 很细心的 + 护士 is the standard shape. 很 + adjective needs 的 before the noun. Putting 很细心的 before 一个 is also heard in speech.

zh: 这是我们小区附近最安静的诊所。
py: zhè shì wǒ men xiǎo qū fù jìn zuì ān jìng de zhěn suǒ
en: This is the quietest clinic near our community.
why: 最 + adjective needs 的: 最安静的诊所. The location 我们小区附近 stays in front, and 的 cannot be dropped after 安静.

zh: 我昨天拍的照片都丢了。
py: wǒ zuó tiān pāi de zhào piān dōu diū le
en: The photos I took yesterday are all lost.
why: The clause 我昨天拍 + 的 sits before 照片. The time word 昨天 may come before or after 我, but the clause must stay before the noun it describes.

zh: 能帮助你睡好觉的手机软件很多。
py: néng bāng zhù nǐ shuì hǎo jiào de shǒu jī ruǎn jiàn hěn duō
en: There are many phone apps that can help you sleep well.
why: The relative clause 能帮助你睡好觉 comes before 手机软件 and ends in 的. There is no 'that' and the clause cannot follow the noun.

zh: 医生开的药很苦。
py: yī shēng kāi de yào hěn kǔ
en: The medicine the doctor prescribed is very bitter.
why: 医生开 + 的 + 药 makes 'the medicine the doctor prescribed', and the whole noun phrase is the subject of 很苦. 的 must come before 药.

zh: 这个手机壳是我的。
py: zhè ge shǒu jī ké shì wǒ de
en: This phone case is mine.
why: 是 + owner + 的 means 'is mine'. The noun is not repeated, but 的 cannot be left out, or the sentence would say the case is me.

zh: 我要大的不要小的。
py: wǒ yào dà de bú yào xiǎo de
en: I want the big one, not the small one.
why: Each 的 stands for the missing noun: 大的 and 小的. English adds 'one', but Chinese keeps 的 alone, and 不要 comes before 小的.

zh: 包里有穿的也有用的。
py: bāo lǐ yǒu chuān de yě yǒu yòng de
en: There are things to wear and things to use in the bag.
why: 穿的 and 用的 are 'things to wear' and 'things to use'. 的 ends each verb and stands for the unnamed things, so there is no noun after it.

zh: 我的两个同事都感冒了。
py: wǒ de liǎng gè tóng shì dōu gǎn mào le
en: Two of my colleagues both have colds.
why: The owner comes first: 我的 + 两个 + 同事. 两个我的同事 is the English-influenced order that Chinese does not use. 都 comes right before the verb.

zh: 我昨天买的那个手机壳很好看。
py: wǒ zuó tiān mǎi de nà ge shǒu jī ké hěn hǎo kàn
en: The phone case I bought yesterday is very nice.
why: The clause 我昨天买的 normally comes before 那个 + noun. The reverse order, 那个我昨天买的手机壳, is also correct, but 的 still ends the clause.

zh: 医生开了三种药。
py: yī shēng kāi le sān zhǒng yào
en: The doctor prescribed three kinds of medicine.
why: The number + measure word 三种 goes straight before 药 with no 的. 了 follows the verb because the object is counted.

zh: 这几个软件我都不会用。
py: zhè jǐ gè ruǎn jiàn wǒ dōu bú huì yòng
en: I don't know how to use any of these apps.
why: 这几个 sits directly before 软件 with no 的. Topic-fronting the object is common, and 我 may come before or after the topic phrase.

src: 小王有一个手机。手机很新。

src: 我妈妈有一个朋友。她是医生。
